theorem_title: Long-Wagner Theorem 1.10 at $d = 3$: the conjecture holds for unions of layers
natural_language_statement:
For every $n \ge 4$, a cube-free $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/2^n\mathbb{Z}$ that is a union of layers satisfies $8|A| \le 5 \cdot 2^n$.

The layers partition $\mathbb{Z}/2^n\mathbb{Z}$ by 2-adic valuation. The extremal set $L_1 \cup L_3$ is itself a union of layers.
source: Jason Long and Adam Zsolt Wagner, "The largest projective cube-free subsets of Z_{2^n}", arXiv:1810.01225, https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.01225, Theorem 1.10, specialized to $d = 3$
